The photo is shrunk to a small thumbnail, the white frame from the original is lost, and the spacing is uneven, but nothing collides. B has the same problems and is worse: the big quote mark butts right against 'PEOPLE', and the small one is jammed against the photo's edge. Both are real collisions, and they leave a dead gap between the two.

The two candidates look pixel-identical. In both, the headline is pushed tight against the top and left edges, and 'FESTIVAL' wraps onto its own third line, which weakens the original's two-line lockup. The photo crop also loses the white chairs and the staircase, so the image is mostly blank wall. The blue and black info boxes are bunched on the right with uneven margins and leave the lower-left quarter empty. The text is readable and the brand colours survive, but the layout needs a designer's fixes before it ships.

A and B are pixel-identical and share the same flaws. The headline is squeezed into a narrow panel at one word per line ('Win / a / study / grant'). 'by submitting to' and 'Xavier Sport Program' are left-aligned under a centred headline, and 'by' is orphaned on its own line. A stray blue bar sticks out of the panel across the tennis ball. The divider lines are broken off and floating outside the panel. The photo is a blurry, over-cropped upscale. The panel runs off the bottom edge with a large empty area beneath the text, and the original's white frame is gone.

Both candidates are practically the same image. In each, the original's thin white frame ended up as a meaningless rectangle hanging over the racket. The two decorative rules have dropped out of place and now look like underlines under 'submitting' and 'Program'. 'by submitting to' is jammed onto one line with 'Xavier Sport Program', which breaks the original's stacked hierarchy. The blue panel runs off the bottom edge, has odd notched top corners and a big empty lower half, and the photo is blurry and over-cropped. The only difference is that the frame sits about 10 px lower in B, so neither is better.

A and B are effectively the same broken layout, and the only difference is where a stray thin line fragment sits. In both, the background photo is a crude, blurry, over-cropped enlargement. A stray blue horizontal bar cuts across the image and makes a cross shape with the narrow blue column. The headline wraps word by word ('Win / a / study / grant'), the 'by submitting to' line is broken into fragments, the divider rules are scattered loose, and there are large dead gaps between the text groups, so neither is usable.

Both share the same flaws. The 'EVENT MANAGMENT' eyebrow has dropped below the headline, flipping the reading order, and it is left-aligned while the headline is centred. The orange owl's top edge is sliced off flat, the confetti is almost gone, and the blue owl is shrunk to a tiny left-hugging afterthought with no balancing element. In A the blue owl is also jammed near the bottom edge under a big empty gap. B moves it up and closes that gap a little, but leaves dead space at the bottom, so it is only marginally better.

Both just shrink the original into a small centred block. That leaves about 60% of the wide banner as blank white on the left and right, so neither was rearranged to fit the new shape, and the 'Award-Winning Architecture' text is tiny and low-contrast at this size. A keeps more of the gold and patterned background visible around the dark box, so it stays closer to the original's look. B makes the box bigger, which hides almost all of the pattern so it reads as a cropped fragment, and its text is barely larger.

Both break the headline into 'CONS TRUC TION' with spaces, which reads as three wrong words. Both shrink the $14.99 price, a key focal point in the original, to tiny fine print below 'only for', and reduce the brick and X graphic to a small icon. B is slightly worse: 'Sets for kids' nearly touches 'Buy 2', and the right-hand cluster is more cramped. A leaves a little more gap between those groups.

Both crop the robot vacuum into an unreadable dark smear, shrink the purple circle (the brand's main shape) to a meaningless sliver in the left corner, and drop the dot pattern and frame line. The 'Smart Home / GADGETS' text is tiny and sits on dark photo instead of on the purple. A at least anchors the text to the right edge, though it's tight against it. B's text floats near the middle with an empty dark area to its right, so the placement looks arbitrary.

Both shrink the side illustrations to tiny thumbnails jammed against the left and right edges under the headline, which leaves the middle of the canvas empty and makes the artwork trivial. Neither one is rearranged for the tall format. In A, 'CREATIVE AGENCY' drifts near the bottom, about 260px from CLAYTONI, so it breaks the logo lockup. B keeps the tagline a little closer, though still loosely grouped, and leaves an empty band at the bottom.

Both split the text into scattered fragments in the left third. 'LYGOM CAFE' and 'www.lygom.se' are very small, the stars are oversized and compete with the headline, and the photo crop cuts off the woman's face. A keeps the subhead together under its rule, with more breathing room. In B, 'with your next cup of coffee' is jammed against 'Only this Christmas', almost colliding with it, and the dashed rules run ragged under the headline, so B looks more cramped and less deliberate.

A: the headline and the red T are stuck in the top half of the canvas, leaving about 40% dead blue space below. In the original the T's stem bled off the bottom edge; here it stops mid-canvas and floats, so the layout looks like a shrunk copy pasted at the top. B: the same T-and-text block is centred vertically, which balances it better, but the T still stops short of the edges instead of bleeding off them, there are empty bands at the top and bottom, and the text block was not scaled up or rearranged for the taller format.

A: the title and subtitle are oversized and sit on top of the busy leaves and dropper bottle. The subtitle 'review' runs into the green bottle and is jammed against the right edge, and the beige brush stroke is cut off from the text and floats on its own. B: it has the same detached brush-stroke fragment and still puts text over the leaves, and its lighter brown lowers the contrast, but the subtitle fits inside the canvas without hitting the bottle, so it is slightly less broken.

A: the beige brush-stroke panel has come loose from the title. It floats in the upper half as a blank shape with stray dark artifact marks, the 'Weekly SPA items review' subtitle is almost as big as 'Spa Utopia', the bottom ~110px is empty, and the product photo is cropped down to unreadable fragments with none of the bottles left. B has almost the same layout and the same faults (oversized subtitle, empty bottom, lost products, jagged brush edge), but its brush panel reaches further down toward the title, so a little more of the original's 'title on a brush stroke' look survives.

Both shrink the crowd illustration into a thin, hard-cropped strip at the top where the figures are tiny and the hard edges look clipped. Both also set the quote in 9 lines with very loose leading, leave dead space at the bottom and pack the two attribution lines too tightly. A is worse because the red attribution sits almost against 'THAT EVER HAS.' with no separating gap. B leaves a clear gap there and uses the space slightly better, so its grouping and hierarchy read more cleanly.

Both are the same shrunk copy of the original: the two decorative clusters are pushed out to the far edges and scaled down. That leaves wide empty yellow bands between them and the centre. The SALE circles and the 'NEW YEAR SPECIAL' headline are tiny for this banner, so the message is weak and it does not read left to right. B sets the headline higher, close to the top edge, with a looser gap above the SALE stack. A gives the headline a little more top margin, so it is marginally better balanced.

Both candidates are broken in the same way. In each, the SALE letters are tiny and slip out of their huge white circles: they sit on the circle edges or the gaps between circles, so the main message can't be read. 'NEW YEAR SPECIAL' is small, floats on the left and is detached from the lantern stack. The decoration is split into two arbitrary clusters, the bottom-left half is crowded while the top-left and bottom are empty, and the original's symmetric centred composition is lost. The only real difference is that B's lantern stack sits about 40px further right, closer to the canvas edge, and A's sits closer to the decor cluster. Neither is better for that, so I'm calling it a tie.

Both break the core SALE motif. The red letters have come loose from their white circles, which now sit in a tiny, empty vertical stack in the middle. The lanterns and clouds are shrunk into illegible clumps that collide with the letters. A's S-A-L-E reads slightly better: the spacing is still uneven and the L and E differ in size, but they are less jammed. In B, L and E sit almost touching at the right edge, so the word does not read as 'SALE'.

Both have the same broken layout. The small doodles (arrow, bulb, question mark, atom) are crammed in a row across the man's face and mouth. The 'PODCAST WITH HARRY LEE HOFFMAN' subtitle sits far off in the top-right corner, cut off from the headline it belongs to. The molecule drawing is oversized and competes with the headline for attention. In A, 'HOW IT WORKS?' butts right up against the cheek and smile. B moves the headline slightly right, so it clears the face a bit better, but its doodles still collide with the face.

Both are nearly the same broken leaderboard. The original's warm orange overlay is lost: the background is a dark, busy crowd photo with a random orange vertical stripe. 'RICHMOND HIGH SCHOOL THEATRE PRESENTS' is crushed to tiny text with one word per line. The play icon is blown up into the largest element and competes with the 'Pygmalion' title. The ticket text sits directly on the busy photo. A shrinks the frame graphic into a tiny box floating next to the title, which is meaningless. B's frame lines are cut-off fragments that butt against the 'g' of 'Pygmalion', which looks like a near-collision, so A is marginally cleaner.

The two candidates are almost identical, and both have the same faults. The cross has drifted off the centred text axis and sits orphaned near x≈390, at the right edge of the text column. The mountain illustration is pushed into the bottom-right corner with a hard, flat-cropped left edge, leaving the upper right and lower left as dead space. A spaces the invite copy, dates and 'Worship & Bible Study' evenly. B squeezes the dates up under the invite copy and leaves a big uneven gap above 'Worship', so A is marginally tidier.

A breaks the headline along the phrase (KEEP CALM / AND / GET A CAT), so it reads naturally, but the lone 'AND' line is a weak middle beat. Its cat cluster has a hard flat bottom edge that floats above the canvas edge instead of bleeding off it like the original, and the top cat's ears nearly touch the top edge. B makes the same illustration mistake (flat cropped base floating above the bottom, cramped at the top) and splits 'KEEP' from 'CALM', leaving an orphaned 'KEEP' that breaks up the slogan, so A is slightly better.

Both just shrink the two elements into a thin leaderboard. The headline is tiny and the cat illustration becomes a small thumbnail stuck to the bottom edge, with large empty purple areas. A pushes the cats far right with a big gap after the text, which leaves the empty left side unbalanced. B groups the text and cats as one centred cluster, which balances better, but it still leaves dead space at both ends and keeps the same weak, shrunken hierarchy.

A: the oversized quote-mark glyph is jammed right up against the first line of the quote. The three-line quote runs nearly from the top edge to the bottom edge and almost touches the G.M. ALLEN box, while the photo is a tiny thumbnail with a stray small glyph next to it. B: the quote, author box and thumbnail have sensible gaps and line up on the vertical centre. However, the two decorative glyphs are blown up and left floating in an empty middle area as competing focal points, the photo is too small to read, and the text is still tight against the top and bottom edges.

A: the enlarged quote-mark block is jammed right up against 'PEOPLE'/'LIVE', which reads as a collision. Its small mark also floats loose next to the photo. B uses the same leaderboard structure (photo, quote, author button reading left to right) and leaves clean space between the marks and the text. In both, the decorative marks are blown up far past their size in the original and compete with the quote, the photo is a tiny cropped thumbnail, and the white frame and the original's open whitespace are mostly lost.

A and B look the same. In both, the headline wraps so that 'FESTIVAL' sits alone on the third line, and the headline is jammed against the left edge of the canvas. The blue info box and the black box are both flush with the right edge, with no margin. The bottom-left of the photo is left as empty dead space, and the small body copy in the boxes is borderline readable at 300px.

A and B look pixel-for-pixel identical, and both have the same faults. The blue panel is too narrow, so 'Win a study grant' breaks one word per line. A stray blue bar sticks out of the panel across the tennis ball to the right edge. The centred headline sits above left-aligned 'by submitting to' and 'Xavier Sport Program' copy. The divider and frame lines are broken off and out of place, the photo is blurry from upscaling, and the bottom of the panel is empty dead space.

I couldn't separate these two; they are nearly pixel-identical and share the same flaws. In both, the thin white frame floats on its own over the racket instead of enclosing the design, the blue panel runs off the bottom edge with a notched top and a large empty lower half, and the divider rules have slipped under 'submitting' and 'Program' so they look like stray underlines. Also, 'by submitting to' and 'Xavier Sport Program' are crammed onto one line, and the photo is badly upscaled and blurry. The only visible difference is the frame's position (about 10 px higher in B, with a faint extra line near the top), which doesn't change the result.

The two candidates are practically identical, and both fail in the same ways. The photo is cropped and upscaled until it pixelates, losing the racket and ball composition. A stray blue horizontal bar cuts across the image and forms a cross with the narrow blue column. The headline breaks one word per line ('Win / a / study / grant'). 'by submitting / to' and 'Xavier Sport Program' are left-aligned and far apart, while the headline is centred. The divider rules and the white frame are lost or become stray slivers. The only differences are a few tiny stray line fragments.

The two candidates are almost identical, and both share the same flaws. The 'EVENT MANAGMENT' eyebrow now sits below the headline when it should sit above it, and it is left-aligned under a centred headline. Most of the confetti is gone, and stray confetti fragments are clipped inside the hanging owl's bounding box. Both columns also have large dead white gaps. A leaves the small blue owl floating with empty space beneath it, while B anchors it to the bottom edge as the original does, though B's owl is jammed against that edge and leaves a bigger empty gap above it.

In both candidates the patterned background is shrunk into a narrow strip in the middle, and the left and right thirds of the banner are left as empty white space, so this is a shrink, not a rearrangement for the wide format. The 'Award-Winning Architecture' text is tiny in both. In A, the dark panel covers almost all of the gold and grey brush pattern, so the original's look is mostly lost. B shows more of the pattern around a smaller panel, so it keeps the feel slightly better, but its text is just as small.

Both have the same layout and the same faults. The headline reads 'CONS TRUC TION' because the original's line breaks were turned into spaces, which breaks the word. The $14.99 price is tiny and subordinate to 'Buy 2 only for', which reverses the original hierarchy. The brick is shrunk to a thumbnail. 'Sets for kids' and 'Buy 2' are jammed together in a cramped right-hand cluster. B is marginally better because it keeps the blue X behind the brick, while A shows only a small blue fragment; A's 'Sets for kids' also sits tighter against the top edge.

Both are the same weak 320x50 crop. The robot vacuum is cropped to an unrecognisable dark rim. The purple brand circle is cut down to a tiny wedge in the bottom-left corner, and the outline frame and dot pattern are gone. The 'Smart Home / GADGETS' text now sits directly on the wood photo with no purple panel behind it, and it is small. A at least leaves some breathing room on the right. In B the text is pushed hard against the right canvas edge, which looks cramped and accidental.

In both candidates the illustration clusters shrink to tiny thumbnails sitting in a thin strip between the headline and the tagline, and large empty navy bands are left above and below. The original's lively framing is lost and the layout looks shrunk rather than redesigned. A is a little better because 'CREATIVE AGENCY' stays closer to 'CLAYTONI'. In B the tagline drops near the bottom edge, which splits the brand lockup and leaves an even bigger dead gap.

Both throw away the original. The barrel photo is shrunk to a tiny thumbnail, the triangle logo is a speck at the bottom instead of sitting above the name, the torn-paper texture and a black bar float around as meaningless fragments, and the tagline is right-aligned under a centred 'Hobbs Timber', so it breaks the axis. A spreads those fragments over the lower half with big random gaps between them. B at least clusters them into one strip at the bottom, but it leaves huge dead space between the headline, the tagline and that cluster.

Both break the same way. The colourful geometric background is cut down to a thin, mostly covered strip. A blank white box with two stray pink dots sits uselessly on the right. The opening-date line butts right up against the 'THE MINIMALIST' pill, and 'DDG STUDIO PRESENTS' floats on its own with no frame or grouping. B keeps slightly more of the pink and blue pattern visible around the name block, so a little more of the brand survives, but its pill and date line almost touch. A's name block covers nearly all the pattern.

Both banners look almost identical and both are broken. The white frame panel sits off-centre on the left, and the text column spills past the panel's right edge. 'J'adore Paris' breaks out through the top of the frame. The decorative rules have come loose from their text and float as random lines, including one alone at the far left edge. The illustration is broken into scattered pieces with large empty areas between them (a bag and a jar stranded on the right), and the text is small with no real hierarchy. B only moves the bag and jar a few pixels, which doesn't change the result.

Both crop the photo too tightly. Both lose the dropper bottles, capsules and most of the leaves, and both leave the brush-stroke swatch floating as a stray grey blob, detached from the title it used to sit behind. The bottom third is empty dead space in both. A keeps 'Spa Utopia' and its subtitle as a tight, clean group below the glass. In B the headline runs into the glass jar's rim, the subtitle sits too far below it, and the type is jammed against the left edge, so B is worse.

Both use the same broken leaderboard layout. The two food photos, which are the key imagery, have shrunk to thumbnail scraps sitting inside leftover background panels (the peach block and the pasta-pattern tile). The decorative frame is now an empty rectangle, the headline is jammed against the left edge, and the line ornaments float as disconnected fragments. B's pasta illustration is a little larger and its spacing differs slightly, but neither difference changes how well the resize works.

The two layouts are almost identical and both are broken. The quote is jammed into the top of the red panel above a large empty red area. A stray rule line strikes through 'MODERN'. The attribution sits off to the side instead of under the quote. The skyline has shrunk to a small strip inside a separate white box, so it no longer anchors the design, and the frame lines are scattered. B only moves things a few pixels to the right, which doesn't change any of these problems.

The two are almost the same layout. In both, the 'EVENT MANAGEMENT' eyebrow has been pulled away from the headline and left as a tiny red label in the top-left corner. The whole left half is sparse confetti with no content, while both owls and the three-line headline are packed into the right half, so the banner is badly lopsided and has a big empty area. B scales the owls and headline up slightly, which pushes 'KIDS BIRTHDAY STUDIO' tighter against the right edge and squeezes the gap between the brown owl and the 'K' even more. A keeps a bit more right margin, so it is marginally less cramped.

The two candidates are almost identical. In both, the 'EVENT MANAGEMENT' kicker is cut off from its headline and stranded in the top-left corner. The two owls have shrunk to tiny icons squeezed together in the middle, and the brown owl overlaps the blue one. The whole left half is just scattered confetti, so the layout is lopsided: a big empty area on the left and a crowded owl-and-headline block on the right. Neither keeps the original's framing, with an owl on each side of a centred title.

Both use almost the same broken layout. The 'EVENT MANAGEMENT' eyebrow is pinned to the top, far from the 'KIDS BIRTHDAY STUDIO' headline at the bottom, so it reads upside-down in hierarchy. The confetti is shrunk into a tiny strip of specks instead of being spread across the canvas, and the owls sit side by side in the middle with large empty bands above and below. B pulls the owls and headline slightly closer together and leaves a bit more bottom margin, but neither difference is enough to pick a winner.

Both candidates have the same failure. The wind-turbine icon and the red, green and blue triangles are shrunk into a thumbnail-sized strip on the left that you can't read, so the original's key imagery and its framing triangles are effectively gone. The headline is pushed hard against the right edge and is far too big for the layout, and stray diagonal lines float across a large empty lower half. The only differences are where the text and lines sit vertically, which doesn't make either one better.

A and B look identical at this size. In both, the wind-turbine icon, which is the hero image in the original, shrinks to a tiny smudge at the far left, jammed against the left edge and the headline, and loses its cyan circle. The red, green and blue triangles are cut down to unreadable slivers at the edges, and the headline/date block sits slightly left of centre with dead space to the right, so the banner reads as a shrunk copy rather than a left-to-right layout.

Both break the core SALE motif. The red letters are pulled out of their white circles, which are left empty in a tiny column, and S/A/L/E are scattered across the banner between shrunken decoration clusters that are too small to read. The L is also much smaller than the other letters. A keeps the letters spaced apart in reading order, though 'NEW YEAR SPECIAL' sits too close to the left edge. B crams the tiny L into the E and against a decoration cluster, which makes it slightly worse.

The two candidates are almost pixel-identical and fail in the same ways. In both, the SALE circles are pushed to the right edge and the letters have shrunk and dropped out of their discs: 'S' and 'L' sit at the bottom of their circles and 'A' sits on the line between two circles, so the main message can't be read. 'NEW YEAR SPECIAL' is tiny and off-centre at the top, and the decoration is copied twice across the canvas instead of being rearranged, so the hierarchy is gone.

A and B look pixel-identical. In both, the photo is cropped down to an unrecognisable mouth and chin, and the 'HOW IT WORKS?' headline sits right on the face, so text lands on a busy image. The headline and the 'PODCAST WITH HARRY LEE HOFFMAN' line are crammed against each other at a tiny, barely readable size, the doodles are reduced to faint fragments at the right edge, and the face is cut off at the left edge.

Both lose the original's main visual, the diamond photo mosaic. It survives only as one small rectangular photo plus an empty wireframe of diamond outlines in the top right, and the headline divider rule is left orphaned under that grid. Body copy is tiny and floats unaligned, and the vertical URL is cramped against it. In A the date diamond almost touches the photo's right edge. B leaves cleaner gaps between the photo and the date diamond, so it is marginally better, though its body copy sits further from the headline and crowds the URL.

The two candidates are nearly identical, and both are broken in the same ways. The city photo collage, the original's key imagery, has shrunk to a tiny thumbnail beside the body copy and is replaced by an empty white diamond outline. The two brown diamonds are cropped at the top edge and crowd the headline. The body text is far too small to read at this size. B's headline and body are very slightly larger, but not enough to make one clearly better.

A and B look pixel-identical. In both, the cat illustration floats in mid-canvas and its bottom edge is cut flat, where the original bled it off the bottom. That leaves a dead purple band below the cats, and the empty space above and below is lopsided. The headline wraps with 'KEEP' alone on its first line, and 'AND'/'CAT' sit almost against the cats with too little gutter.

I can't see a meaningful difference between the two layouts. Both use the same left-to-right banner: headline, window, then details. In both, the stained-glass window has shrunk to a small icon and is no longer the centrepiece it is in the original. Wide empty gaps separate the three groups, and the headline sits tight against the top and left edges. The date and address text is very small at this height, so both need margin and scale fixes before shipping.

The two candidates are almost identical. In both, the 'EVENT MANAGMENT' eyebrow is pulled far left, away from the headline it labels, and set at a tiny size. The owls are shrunk to small icons and the confetti crowds the purple headline, which leaves a large dead area on the left. In B the eyebrow also sits even closer to the left edge (about 25px versus about 45px in A), so A is only marginally less cramped.

Both break the brand lockup: HOHOHO sits top-left and AGENCY bottom-left, with a jumble of clipped decorative shapes between them (cut-off triangles, a sliced black circle, a stray C ring). The tagline is pushed into a cramped spot on the right, so there is no clear hierarchy or grid. A edges ahead because it breaks the tagline cleanly into 'Office / Secret Santa', while B leaves 'Santa' alone on its own line and packs the text tighter against the tree and the C ring.

A and B are practically the same image; B is only shifted by a pixel or two. Both share the same flaws. The translucent band is narrow and sits left of centre, and it does nothing for contrast. 'Save your money, enjoy your weekend' and both chevron sets sit directly on the busy skyline, so they are hard to read. The text block is small and leaves the top-right and the whole lower half as unused photo, so the result looks like a crop rather than a reworked layout.

Both banners are nearly identical, and both fail in the same way. The hands photo, which is the key image, is gone except for a stray black sliver at the top edge. The quote sits flat on plain white, and the attribution floats far off to the right with no link to the quote. The cross motif is clipped against the right edge as a faint smudge. Almost no trace of the original's dark, moody feel survives in either version.

Both are nearly identical broken layouts. The photo is cut into a narrow center strip with large white dead areas on both sides, and the white cloud shapes float detached on the white left side, where they are almost invisible. A white text box chops off the lower half of the photo and hides the hands, which were the main image. The quote is readable but sits off-center to the right, and nothing lines up on a clear grid. The only difference is the cross: in A it sits slightly higher and stands out more clearly against the dark photo, while B's cross is lost on the hands, so A wins by a hair.

A and B are practically the same, and both are broken in the same ways. 'Smart Home' has slipped off the purple circle and now sits on the busy wood photo, far above 'GADGETS', which splits the headline lockup. 'GADGETS' is jammed against the left canvas edge. The purple circle is shrunk into a small bottom corner. The outline frame stops partway down the canvas and no longer wraps the text. Because of all this, the bottom half reads as scattered fragments instead of an intentional layout.

Both are unusable and almost identical. The bath photo, which carries the original, has shrunk to a tiny thumbnail that floats on its own off-centre. The yellow headline panel sits isolated in the middle of an empty white strip, and its text is tiny. The thin yellow frame is gone, and there are stray yellow slivers at the top-right edge. A is only marginally better because its headline and photo are slightly larger; B is a little smaller and more cramped.

A and B look pixel-identical. In both, the building photo has shrunk to a thin strip pinned to the left edge, and the 'the limit' line runs over it, so headline text sits on a busy image. The top-left is empty, the wrap 'Sky is / not / the limit / for us.' leaves 'not' alone on its own line, and the photo has lost its role as the angled hero image from the original.

Both have the same main flaw. The building photo, the original's key image, is reduced to a thin strip cut off at the left edge. Its pale background band runs behind 'not/the', and the stacked headline breaks into one or two words per line, leaving large empty areas above and below. A is a little better because its text block is vertically centred, with the photo strip level with its middle. B's text sits lower and off-centre, which makes the image look stranded near the top of the headline.

A: the headline lockup sits roughly centred with dot clusters anchoring the bottom corners, so the canvas has some balance. Still, the thin photo strip is stranded at the top with dots overprinting it, large empty bands surround the small title, the right dot cluster is cut off at the edge, and the lockup sits left of centre. B: everything is crammed into the top half (photo strip, headline, dots) and the bottom ~45% is dead navy, so the layout is badly lopsided. The headline is jammed under the strip, and the clipped dot clusters float in the middle with no purpose.

In both, the barrel photo has shrunk to a tiny thumbnail, the logo mark is postage-stamp sized, and a stray black bar and a cut-off texture fragment float in large areas of empty white, so the design is gone. A at least keeps these fragments in one cluster near the bottom. B spreads them down the canvas, with uneven gaps and right-aligned tagline that matches nothing, so it reads even more like scattered debris.

Both break the design the same way. The geometric pattern is cut down to a narrow strip, and an empty white frame holding the two pink dots floats off on the right as dead space. 'DDG STUDIO PRESENTS' sits off to the left and doesn't line up with anything. The 'THE MINIMALIST' pill runs straight into the 'OPENING…' line, so the reading order is jumbled and the poster's structure is gone. B is slightly worse: 'DEAN COOPER' is pushed out to the card's edge and the white block covers more of the pattern, while A leaves a little more of the brand pattern visible.

Both candidates are essentially the same broken layout. The white label frame is pushed left and cut off at the top, and the text block (J'adore Paris / LAVANDER / SKINCARE / HOMEMADE LOTION) has drifted off the frame's centre and onto its right edge. The decorative rules are scattered: one sits beside LAVANDER, another floats loose at the far left, and a third is stranded under the text. The illustrations are broken into small separate clumps with large empty beige gaps, and the frame's bottom is cut off. The only difference is that B moves the sachet and bottle slightly closer together, which changes nothing.

A: the photo is a tight crop that drops the dropper bottles and capsules. The beige brush-stroke swatch floats on its own, cut off from the title, and 'Spa Utopia' sits on the rim of the glass bowl. The subtitle is pushed far below the title and the bottom third is dead space. B: same crop and the same detached swatch, which now also clumsily overlaps the glass bowl. Still, the title is clear of the imagery, the subtitle sits tighter under it and the empty space at the bottom is smaller, so B is slightly less broken.

Both leaderboards break the design the same way. The peach and pasta-pattern background panels have turned into separate boxes, the two hero food photos are shrunk to tiny thumbnails jammed into their top-left corners, and the ornate frame is an empty rectangle. The swash dividers float loose and the headline sits tight against the left and top edges. The only difference is that B nudges the Cascadia/RESTAURANT/URL block slightly, so they are effectively equal and both unusable.

I couldn't find a meaningful difference between the two; B is just the same layout shifted a few pixels left. Both have the same problems: a decorative rule cuts through "MODERN" in the headline, and the quote is jammed against the top of the red panel, leaving a large empty red area below it. The author name floats off to the right instead of sitting under the quote, and the skyline (the key image) has shrunk to a small strip in a separate white box, so the layered skyline-over-panel feel of the original is gone.

Both use the same broken layout. The tiny red 'EVENT MANAGEMENT' sits alone in the top-left corner, far from the headline it introduces. The left half is a shrunken confetti field with no content, while the owls and the three-line headline are packed together on the right with almost no gap between the brown owl and the text. B's owls and headline are slightly larger, but its owl is even closer to 'KIDS BIRTHDAY STUDIO', so neither is meaningfully better.

The two candidates are virtually identical, so neither is the better resize. In both, the 'EVENT MANAGEMENT' eyebrow is cut off from its headline: it sits alone in the top-left while 'KIDS BIRTHDAY STUDIO' is stacked at the far right, which breaks grouping and reading order. The two owls, the original's key imagery, have shrunk to tiny props squeezed against the headline, and the left half is mostly scattered confetti, so the balance is lopsided and the original's playful feel is lost.

Both use the same broken layout. The 'EVENT MANAGEMENT' eyebrow is stranded at the top, far from the 'KIDS BIRTHDAY STUDIO' headline at the bottom, and the confetti is shrunk into a tiny strip, leaving large empty bands. The owls are reduced to a small side-by-side pair in the middle. B is slightly worse because the brown owl crowds closer to the blue owl's hat and its headline sits tighter to the bottom edge.

Both candidates fail the same way. The whole background artwork (green, blue and red triangles, the decorative lines and the wind-turbine icon) has been shrunk into a tiny strip to the left of the headline. The turbine, the design's key image, ends up as an unreadable speck, the bold headline crowds the right edge, and the top half and bottom third are mostly empty. A is very slightly better because its two leftover lines sit together as a pair at the bottom. In B the upper line nearly touches 'MARCH 18' and there is a large awkward gap between the two lines.

A and B look the same. In both, the wind-turbine icon, which was the original's hero image, has shrunk to an unreadable speck crowded against the left end of the headline. The red, green and blue triangles are cut down to stray slivers at the edges, so they read as clutter rather than intentional framing. The headline fills almost the whole width with little side margin, and the line art is lost entirely. Both are still a scaled-down copy of the centred layout instead of a left-to-right banner layout.

Both break the SALE motif: the letters are pulled out of their lantern circles and scattered across the banner, the circles are left empty in the middle, the lantern and cloud artwork is shrunk into tiny clusters, and the 'L' is shrunk far below the other letters, so the word no longer reads as SALE. A is slightly worse because its tiny 'L' is jammed against the 'E'. B at least keeps the letters apart, though its spacing is still arbitrary and the 'L' is still miniature.

The two candidates are almost pixel-identical, and both are broken. The 'SALE' letters have shrunk to tiny glyphs stuck at the bottom of oversized empty circles (the 'A' sits on a circle's lower edge, and in B it lands on the seam between circles). The column of circles is pushed against the right edge, 'NEW YEAR SPECIAL' is a tiny line off-centre at the top, and the decoration is just duplicated to fill the space, so the main message is lost and nothing has a clear hierarchy.

A and B look pixel-identical. In both, the photo is cropped so tightly that only a mouth and chin remain, which loses the key imagery. The 'HOW IT WORKS?' headline sits on top of the face, so the text collides with a busy image. The 'Podcast with Harry Lee Hoffman' copy is tiny, and the question-mark and molecule doodles are cramped against the right edge.

Both lose the original's main feature, the diamond photo mosaic. It shrinks to one small rectangular crop, and an empty grid of white outline diamonds plus a stray divider line hang in the top right as broken leftovers. The body copy is tiny and set apart from the headline, and the vertical URL floats on its own. A spaces the date diamond evenly away from the photo. In B the date diamond almost touches the photo edge, which looks cramped, though B's body copy sits slightly closer to the headline.

The two candidates are almost pixel-identical, and both fail in the same ways. The city photo mosaic, the original's key imagery, has shrunk to a tiny thumbnail beside the body copy, leaving bare brown diamonds and empty line-work. The address in the left diamond and the body paragraph are tiny and hard to read, the headline rule and the vertical URL are gone, and the diamonds dominate over the headline in an unbalanced layout.

A and B are practically identical, so this is a tie. Both use a sensible two-column banner layout, but they share the same flaws. The cat illustration, which bled off the bottom edge in the original, now ends in a hard flat crop floating above the canvas bottom, so it looks like a pasted rectangle. 'KEEP' sits alone on its line, leaving an awkward 1/2/1 word break. The cats are shrunk to a small cluster, which leaves large empty purple margins above and below.

The two are practically identical: both keep the left-to-right headline / stained-glass window / details layout for the leaderboard and the brand survives. In both, the headline sits right against the top edge with almost no margin, the window is shrunk into a small icon that has lost its role as the centrepiece, and the date and address lines are tiny and hard to read at this size.

Both use the same broken layout. The 'EVENT MANAGMENT' eyebrow is stranded far left, cut off from the headline it belongs with. The headline sits in a scatter of confetti. The upside-down owl is cropped at the top, and the blue owl is tiny and pushed into the far-right corner. A large dead area sits on the left. The only difference is that B gives the eyebrow a slightly more comfortable left margin, while A's is tighter against the canvas edge.

Both candidates break the 'HOHOHO AGENCY' lockup: HOHOHO sits top-left and AGENCY bottom-left, with a scattered band of cropped, cut-off decorative fragments between them. This leaves no clear focal point, and the tagline looks to have lost its italic styling. A wraps the tagline badly ('Office Secret / Santa' leaves an orphaned word), and the text crowds the blue C shape. B's 'Office / Secret Santa' wraps a little better, but it is still a jumbled, disordered layout.

A and B are practically identical; B's text block is shifted only a couple of pixels. Both have the same problems. The translucent vertical band is now a narrow strip off to the right of centre, so 'London' and the tagline run past both of its edges. 'Save your money, enjoy your weekend' sits right on top of the busy skyline with weak contrast. The '<<<' and '>>>' chevrons float in arbitrary spots and no longer frame the copy. The cropped photo is soft and upscaled, and the lower half of the canvas is unused city texture, so this reads as a crop rather than a deliberate re-layout.

Both candidates are essentially the same broken layout. The praying-hands photo, which is the key image, is gone entirely, along with the cloud shape. A stray black rectangle sits clipped at the top centre, and the faint plus-sign crosses are pushed off the right edge. The quote and the 'Mahatma Gandhi' credit float far apart on a blank white strip. The only difference is a slightly different placement of the cut-off crosses, so neither is better.

A and B are essentially the same broken layout. In both, the photo is cropped to a narrow centre strip, and a white text panel covers the praying hands, which are the key image. The cloud graphic floats loose on a white field on the left with no edge, and the left third of the canvas is dead space. Only the small plus sign is placed slightly differently, and that is not enough to pick a winner. The quote text is readable, but the original's dark image flowing into the cloud is lost.

The two candidates are almost identical. In both, 'Smart Home' has moved off the purple circle and sits on the wood-grain photo, so the headline is split across two backgrounds. 'GADGETS' runs nearly edge to edge and is jammed against the canvas sides. The purple circle has shrunk to a small blob in the bottom corner, and the outline frame floats on its own, cut off above the text, instead of enclosing the type as it does in the original. B's frame sits slightly lower and more centred than A's, but that difference is negligible.

Both candidates are unusable. They have the same failures: the hero photo of the mother and child is shrunk to a tiny thumbnail floating on the left, and the yellow 'LOVE. CARE. KIDS.' panel is a small sliver in the middle of a mostly empty white banner. The headline text is barely readable, the thin yellow frame and accent bars are gone or reduced to specks in the corner, and nothing has been rearranged for a left-to-right banner. B is only marginally less bad because its headline text in the yellow panel is slightly larger.

A and B look pixel-identical. Both shrink the building photo to a thin strip cropped at the left edge, and the 'the limit' line collides with it, so text sits on a busy image. The headline's leading is so tight that the 'y' descender touches 'not', the line breaks are awkward with 'not' alone on its own line, and the top-left quadrant is a large dead area, which unbalances the square layout.

Both candidates are nearly identical, and both have the same problems. The building photo, the original's main image, is shrunk to a small wedge cut off at the left edge, with a faint grey band trailing behind the text. The headline wraps into five ragged lines, leaving 'not' and 'the' as single-word lines, and the descender of 'y' in 'Sky' touches 'not'. Large areas of empty white space sit above and below. B is slightly less bad because its text block is vertically centred on the image strip and the canvas, while A's text sits low, leaving a big empty area at the top and a cramped bottom.

A packs the image strip and the '& Baby Toddler BEDDING' lockup into the top third. Its dot grids float in the middle, and the bottom ~45% of the canvas is empty, so the layout is badly top-heavy. B is the less bad one: it centres the lockup vertically and anchors the dot grids in the bottom corners, which balances the frame better. B still has large dead bands above and below the headline, and in both the image strip is a small, cropped sliver with the dot pattern sitting on top of it.

Both reduce the photo to an unreadable strip of sweater at the right edge, and the 'GIFT' and 'cup of coffee' text runs onto it, so text sits on a busy image. 'Only this Christmas' is pushed off-centre while the stars sit at the left, there is a stray line at the bottom-left, and 'next' is left alone on its own line. A spaces its dashed dividers unevenly but keeps the headline slightly clearer of the pattern. B groups the elements a bit more tightly but drops 'GIFT' right onto the red-and-white pattern, so the two are close to equal.

A and B look pixel-identical and both are broken. The patterned background is a narrow strip floating in the middle with white dead space on the right. The white frame is shrunk into an empty box on the right holding stray pink dots, and the white text panel cuts across the pattern. 'THE MINIMALIST' and the opening date are tiny and crammed into one bottom row, and the original's centred, framed composition is lost.

Both are the same broken layout. The pink dots crash into the 'DEAN' headline. 'DDG STUDIO PRESENTS' has dropped below the name, so the reading order is wrong. The 'OPENING…' line runs against the left edge. The pattern has shrunk to a cropped band, with an empty white frame and dead white space below it. B is shifted further up, which leaves an even larger empty bottom third and makes the canvas more lopsided, so A is very slightly less unbalanced.

Both break apart the original's main idea: the red T no longer sits behind the copy and ends up as an unrelated block on the far right. The headline is shrunk to tiny five-line stacked text that runs almost from the top edge to the bottom edge, and most of the banner in between is empty blue. A also floats the text at an arbitrary inset with dead space on its left, and its spacing in 'AGAINSTCRUELTY' looks wrong. B is slightly better because it anchors the text to a consistent left margin and keeps the word spacing correct.

A and B are almost pixel-identical and have the same breakage. The rules that should frame LAVANDER are shifted right, so they start at the centre and run off past the text. The rules beside HOMEMADE LOTION have come apart: the left one floats over the lavender sprig and the right one hangs near the vase. The type is also far too small for the wide canvas: SKINCARE is barely legible and the headline is weak inside a large empty frame. The illustration row is just stretched across the bottom rather than rearranged.

Both crush all the supporting copy (tagline, green feature line, phone, website) into a right-hand column of type about 4px tall. At 320×50 it can't be read, and the right side is overstuffed while the headline floats on the left. A breaks the headline more evenly ('Traditional / Ceramics Workshop') and keeps its dash dividers clear. B leaves 'Workshop' alone on the second line, and its right column wraps one more line so it presses against the top and bottom edges.

The two candidates are almost the same. In both, the orange headline is left-aligned and shifted right while the rest of the text is centred. The teal 'Great location' line is pushed right and nearly touches the right edge. The contact block is crammed toward the bottom with loose line spacing. A edges ahead because its contact lines are more even in length. B breaks after 'phone', which leaves a short phone-number line under a long line, and B's dashed dividers sit a little further off-centre.

A: the 'Spa Utopia' title sits right on top of the busy product photo (bottle, capsule, glass), and the tagline is cut through by dark leaf stripes so it can barely be read. The original's soft blush backing swatch behind the text is gone, and the whole thing reads like a crop with text dropped on top. B has the same core faults: the title runs into the green bottle near the left edge, and the tagline sits on the white dropper and leaves. Its larger, bolder title gives it slightly clearer hierarchy, which is the only reason it edges out A.

A pushes the maroon panel to the top, so the X mark is jammed against the canvas edge and overlaps the panel's corner. The lower half is dead photo space, with the slash and circle drifting far from the panel they used to frame. B centres the panel and balances the canvas better, but the corner marks are still scattered: the bottom slash and circle float detached below the panel. In both, the text block is small for the tall format, the 'Join WADE team' CTA is weak, and the photo crop loses the readable meeting-table scene.

I can't see a real difference between the two. Both enlarge the maroon panel cleanly and keep the type hierarchy and brand, but they share the same flaws. The bottom slash and circle sit about 115px below the panel's bottom edge, so they no longer frame its corners the way the top X and slash do. The panel also has a large empty gap between the rule and 'Join WADE team', and that line now sits on top of the clasped hands at the bottom left. The only change is that the circle sits a few pixels differently in B, which doesn't affect quality.

Both shrink the owls into a small cramped pair beside the headline, losing the original's large framing mascots, and squeeze the confetti into a flat band instead of scattering it across the canvas. In B, the 'EVENT MANAGEMENT' eyebrow is pushed to the top edge, far from the headline, and a large empty gap sits in the middle. A keeps the eyebrow closer to the headline and the stack sits nearer the centre, but it still has dead space at the top and bottom, and the confetti band separates the eyebrow from its headline.

In both, the wind-turbine hero icon is shrunk to a tiny glyph and squeezed into a cramped row of tiny triangles and line fragments at the top. That throws away the original's centred icon-over-title composition, and the brand shapes become trivial. The headline is broken into one word per line, which reads choppily. A leaves more room between that top strip and the headline and sits the text nearer the vertical centre. B pushes the headline right up against the strip and leaves a larger empty area at the bottom with only stray lines in it.

The two candidates look pixel-identical, so they share the same flaws. The wind-turbine icon, which is the hero image in the original, has shrunk to a tiny glyph and sits wedged between the green, blue and red triangles. Those triangles are cramped into an awkward strip along the top edge. The headline is oversized and crowds the left and bottom edges, which buries the imagery and reverses the original's icon-first hierarchy. The stray diagonal lines float at random on the right.

A: the heart monster, bell, candy cane and gifts are jammed into one colliding knot against the M of MERRY. DISCOUNT runs straight into the small monsters, and the right side is an overstuffed run (holly on the red monster, ghost, tall monster) that hits the canvas edge. On top of that, DISCOUNT is tiny at this height. B has the same weak structure: small DISCOUNT, illustrations crowding the headline, gifts and candy cane pressed against the M, and the bell touching the heart monster. Its characters are spaced a little more evenly, with breathing room before the last monster, so it is the less cramped of the two.

A reflows sensibly into a left-to-right banner: MERRY and DISCOUNT sit side by side with a clear gap, and the characters are spread along both sides. Its flaws: the heart creature is jammed against the top edge, the right-edge green monster is crowded against the canvas edge, and the small DISCOUNT text loses force in a busy strip. In B, the candy cane and gift box collide with the M of MERRY, the Y nearly touches DISCOUNT, and the heart creature crowds the top of DISCOUNT, so the headline cluster looks cramped while there is dead space further right.

A and B are almost pixel-identical and both unusable. The background stays a narrow centred portrait strip with white dead space on either side. The headline overflows that strip, so 'Special' and 'Int-' disappear as white text on white, and 'Joint celebration & Forest cleanup' is cut off. The quote and URL copy are missing, the divider line is stranded on white at the right, and 'March 21' sits on the pale sky band. The only difference is that 'March 21' sits a few pixels higher in B, which doesn't matter.

The two candidates are almost pixel-identical and share the same flaws. The original's full-bleed stripes behind a white card have become three small separate bars stuck on the left, so the brand composition is lost. The copy is broken into scattered pieces with no grid: the 'for all drinkware on' fragment is tiny, wraps awkwardly and floats at the bottom left, and the vertical URL is too small to read and stranded in the middle. The product list sits off on its own at the right, leaving dead white space throughout.

The two are almost identical. Each puts the two-line headline on the left and squeezes the cat illustration, the original's hero image, into a small cluster at the right edge, leaving a dead purple gap between them. At 50 px tall the cats are barely readable, so the illustration becomes trivial. A's cats are slightly larger and bleed off the bottom edge as in the original, which keeps a little more of the imagery's presence. B's cats are smaller and its cluster sits a bit closer to the headline, which makes the right side look more like an afterthought.

The two candidates are almost identical, and both share the same flaws. The top-left ■▌ mark is blown up far beyond its size in the original, so it competes with the quote. The photo sits flush left and leaves an awkward empty strip on its right. The G.M. ALLEN box is indented and doesn't line up with the quote's left edge, and the bottom mark floats with no clear alignment. A has slightly less room between the quote and the attribution box, so it looks more cramped; B spaces the quote, attribution box and bottom mark a little more evenly, but its bottom mark is slightly off the box's left edge.

Both are blurry, upscaled crops that lose the brand's defining multicoloured 'ART' letterforms: only a black 'T' fragment and some pink stripes remain, so the design is barely recognisable. The headline is readable but wraps badly ('NOT A / HOBBY'), and neither candidate rearranges the design. A leaves the bottom half almost empty apart from a stray tan bar and a sliver of yellow, which makes it badly lopsided. B's stripes are cut off top and bottom, and pink slivers and a tan block sit right under 'LIFE.' like slicing artifacts, but its weight is spread slightly more evenly.

Both are near-identical uniform shrinks of the original. The headline, stained-glass window and date/address block keep the original left-to-right order without collisions, but the right-hand date/address text drops to a very small size and is hard to read in the short canvas. In A the window sits slightly high, with a tight top margin and more empty space below, so it is off-centre from the text. B centres the window a touch better vertically, so the two are otherwise equivalent.

The two resizes are nearly identical. Both crop the blue photo into a thin, unreadable strip at the top, and in both 'Baby Toddler' runs into the right-hand dot pattern. A also leaves a dead gap between the photo and the ampersand, while 'BEDDING' sits low near the bottom edge, apart from the ampersand group. B pulls 'BEDDING' up so it forms a tighter group with the ampersand, which gives better grouping and an even bottom margin.

A and B look pixel-identical. In both, the illustrated figures are shrunk to tiny clusters at the left and right edges halfway down. 'CLAYTONI' sits at the very top and 'CREATIVE AGENCY' is separated from it at the very bottom, so the logo lockup is split up and there is a huge empty navy area in between. Neither one rearranges the design for the tall skyscraper shape, and the original's colourful character artwork is reduced to almost nothing.

Both are nearly identical skyscraper resizes. In each, the photo is cropped down to a sliver of sweater, so the woman, mug and gift box are gone, and the headline 'A GIFT' runs onto the busy knit pattern. Both also have a ragged layout: the centered cafe logo and copy sit against a left-hung 'Only this Christmas' and stars, the URL is pushed right, and 'with your next' breaks awkwardly onto its own line. A has slightly more even vertical spacing. B jams the headline up under the gift icons and leaves a large gap below the dashed rule.

A and B look the same; they differ by a pixel or two at most. Both are broken in the same ways. The geometric background is squeezed into a narrow middle strip, leaving bare white on the left and right. The white frame has slid off to the right and sits in empty space, and the pink dots are stranded in the pattern and in the empty area instead of flanking the name. 'THE MINIMALIST' and the opening line are tiny and wedged into one ragged row at the bottom, pushed against the left edge, so the hierarchy and centred symmetry of the original are lost.

Both are nearly identical and broken. The reading order is scrambled: 'THE MINIMALIST' sits above the name and 'DDG STUDIO PRESENTS' below it. The pink dots run into the D and N of DEAN. The white text panel cuts across the top of the geometric graphic, and the 'OPENING…' line is jammed against the left edge and the white frame. The frame is left hanging over an empty white area, so the bottom of the canvas is dead space. A leaves a much larger empty area at the bottom (about 30% of the height), with all the text crammed at the top. B is centred a little better vertically, but its panel covers more of the graphic, so it is only marginally less lopsided.

The two are almost identical and both fail. Each keeps the five-line stacked headline in tiny type that nearly touches the top and bottom edges, when this banner shape calls for one line of larger text. Each also pulls the red T off to the right, losing the original's layered text-on-T effect and leaving a huge empty band in the middle. A pins the text block to the far left, so its dead gap is even bigger. B moves the text in a little, which makes the gap smaller but leaves an arbitrary empty strip on the left, and its 'AGAINST CRUELTY' line looks cramped.

Both have the same broken decorative rules. The lines meant to frame LAVANDER start at its centre and run off to the right edge of the panel, and the rules beside HOMEMADE LOTION are pulled apart: the left one cuts across a lavender sprig and the right one floats by itself. In both, the text block is tiny for the wide canvas and SKINCARE is almost unreadable. The two candidates are nearly pixel-identical; B is only shifted a few pixels to the right.

Both are near-identical 320x50 banners. The orange headline sits on the left, and the body copy, tagline, dashed divider and booking/URL text are crammed into a column on the right at about 4–5px. That text is unreadable, there is no clear CTA, and the dividers are just clutter. A edges ahead because its 'Traditional Ceramics / Workshop' headline is larger and anchors the hierarchy better. B breaks it 'Traditional / Ceramics Workshop' at a smaller size, which makes it weaker. B's right column is no more legible than A's.

Both are nearly identical tall reflows with the same flaws. The orange title is left-offset while every other element is centred, and the white body copy is now bigger than the title, which inverts the hierarchy. The teal line juts toward the right edge and the contact block runs close to the bottom. A wins narrowly because it breaks the contact copy naturally ('Book your place now by phone' / number), while B splits it awkwardly at 'by / phone'. A's dashed dividers sit slightly right of centre, which is a minor flaw.

A: 'Spa Utopia' runs over the green dropper bottle on the left. The 'Weekly SPA items review' subtitle is set tiny, in a cramped two-line wrap, on top of busy leaf stems, so it can't be read at 320x50, and the original's brush-stroke backing is lost. B has the same problems and is a little worse: the headline sits on the glass dish, and the subtitle lands on the cream jar rim and leaves with even less contrast, so it is essentially unreadable.

A keeps the maroon panel and its copy intact and sits it roughly in the middle of the canvas. However, the decorative X, slashes and circle are scattered and no longer frame the panel's corners as they do in the original, and the crop cuts off the people around the table. The text is also small for the size. B pushes the panel up against the top, so the X collides with its corner and the bottom ~270px is empty photo with loose marks, which makes the layout top-heavy and less balanced than A.

The two are nearly identical. Both keep the maroon overlay and the type hierarchy, but the overlay stops around y≈575. That leaves the bottom corner marks (slash and circle) floating over the photo, detached from the box they are supposed to frame. Inside the box there is also a large dead gap between the rule and 'Join WADE team'. In A the bottom marks sit even lower (y≈690), with the circle over a man's head. B's marks are slightly closer to the box, so the misalignment is a little less severe.

A: 'EVENT MANAGEMENT' is pushed up against the top edge, about 400px away from its headline, so the two no longer read as a group. The confetti is packed into the upper third, leaving a large dead band in the middle and empty space at the bottom. The owls have shrunk to tiny icons that compete with the headline instead of framing it. B has the same tiny owls, compressed confetti block and empty top and bottom bands. It still scores higher because the kicker, confetti and headline form one tighter vertical group, even though the kicker is still far from the title and the layout feels like a shrunk copy of the original.

Both make the same serious mistakes. The wind-turbine icon, which is the hero image, has been shrunk to a tiny glyph. It sits in a cramped strip at the top beside squashed coloured triangles and stray diagonal lines, so the original's airy triangles at the corners are lost. The title is huge and wraps into a narrow column with one word per line, which pushes the icon down to a minor detail, and the lower half is mostly leftover diagonal lines in empty space. A sits the title high against the icon strip and leaves a larger empty area at the bottom. B gives the title more room below the strip and spreads the weight a little more evenly, so it is slightly less lopsided.

A and B look pixel-identical, so this is a tie. Both have the same flaws. The wind-turbine icon, which is the original's hero image, has shrunk to a tiny unreadable mark at the top. The coloured triangles are squeezed into a small row of fragments across the top edge, with stray line segments scattered around them. The headline wraps into an oversized four-line block with no balance. The decorative lines on the right crowd the ends of 'SUMMIT' and 'MARCH 18', and there is dead space at the bottom.

A: 'MERRY' is crowded by the heart-monster, bell, candy cane and gifts, which collide with it on the left; 'DISCOUNT' runs right into the small monsters; the characters are squeezed into a cluttered strip with uneven gaps, such as the empty space before the star monster, and the text is tiny. B has the same 'MERRY' collisions with the bell, candy cane and gifts, plus a dead gap after the yeti on the left and a jammed right cluster where the red monster, holly, ghost and star monster pile into each other, so it looks slightly more chaotic.

I'd ship neither as is, but B is the better resize. In A, the gift stack and candy cane run into the 'M' of MERRY, the green heart creature crowds the gap between MERRY and DISCOUNT, and the right-hand group (red monster, ghost, green monster) is piled into overlaps. B gives the candy cane and gifts their own space beside MERRY and spreads the characters more evenly, but the heart creature still sits almost on top of DISCOUNT, the ghost overlaps the green monster, and the headline is too small for a 728×90 banner to be the clear focal point.

A and B are essentially the same broken output, and both are unusable. The background only fills a narrow center strip on a white canvas. The white headline runs off the image onto the white area, so it reads only as 'Event Devo… / ernational D… / f Forests'. The subhead is cut off ('ration & Forest clea'), and one divider line floats loose on the right. The quote, the URL/call to action and the second divider are missing. The only visible difference is that 'March 21' sits a few pixels lower in B.

The two layouts are almost identical and both are broken. The white card is gone, so the copy is scattered across a white field with no grouping. 'for all drinkware on' is a tiny wrapped fragment, cut off from $49.99 and placed bottom-left. The vertical URL is microscopic and unreadable. The colour stripes are boxed into a separate block on the left with large dead gaps between the pieces. A's 'for all' looks squeezed into 'forall', while B's letter spacing is slightly cleaner, so B wins by a hair.
